name: mcp
description: Returns the live handle for the MCP call in flight. Only available inside an MCP tool, resource, or prompt handler. The handle lets a long-running tool report progress, emit structured logs, inspect the client and session, ask the client for sampling or input, and send tool-change notifications. Each handle method returns a boolean saying whether the notification was actually delivered, so a tool can tell when nobody is listening.

links.title: RustCFML MCP documentation
links.description: Full documentation of the RustCFML Model Context Protocol support, including the mcp() handle.

examples.title: Report progress and log from a streaming tool
examples.description: Inside a tool that declares streaming=true, use mcp() to push progress notifications and structured log messages back to the client.

examples.title: Inspect the client and session
examples.description: mcp().session(), mcp().server(), mcp().client(), and mcp().streaming() expose the conversation/server identifiers, the client's initialize details and capabilities, and whether this call has a stream.
